MODEL_FEEDBACK_JSON:
{
  "positive_alignment_reasons": [
    "Dark Side Of The Moon feels like a natural next listen after my classic rock collections and Sgt. Pepper's because I want familiar melodies and an absorbing full album.",
    "Partners connects with my interest in the vocal duets on Cheek to Cheek, while 25 appeals through expressive singing and melodic pop."
  ],
  "negative_misalignment_reasons": [
    "Hybrid Theory, St. Anger, and Master of Puppets emphasize a heavier, more aggressive sound than the melodic classic rock and folk I want now.",
    "American Idiot and Appetite For Destruction share a broad rock connection with my listening, but their energy and harder edge do not match my current mood.",
    "Adele's 21 appeals to me too, but I would choose only one Adele album this time; liking both does not mean I want both now."
  ],
  "overgeneralized_signals": [
    "My interest in classic rock seems to have been taken as interest in rock of any intensity, even though gentler melodies matter to my choices today.",
    "My listening to Born This Way seems to have been stretched into an appetite for high energy music more broadly, which does not explain my interest in aggressive rock or metal."
  ],
  "missing_or_underweighted_signals": [
    "Simon & Garfunkel, Jonathan Edwards, and Melanie suggest that tuneful songs and gentler folk sounds deserve more attention in what I might choose next.",
    "Cheek to Cheek points toward expressive vocals and duets, a connection that makes Partners appealing beyond simply being another familiar album."
  ],
  "summary_diagnosis": "The choices partly capture my interest in classic albums and expressive vocals, but stretch my rock listening too far toward aggression and intensity."
}
